level_m.description: finished elevation of the planting surface. Set it when the bed sits on a cut/filled terrace bench (normally the same level as the path and retaining edge beside it); omit to let the bed follow existing ground.

material.description: free text; flagstone, paver, gravel, decomposed_granite, concrete, stepping_stones are modelled and render as themselves, anything else draws as the nearest surface and is recorded as a want

level_m.description: finished elevation of the walking surface. Set it when the path is cut/filled to a level bench (retained by edging); omit to follow existing ground.

material.description: free text; flagstone, paver, gravel, decomposed_granite, concrete, stepping_stones, deck, lawn are modelled and render as themselves, anything else draws as the nearest surface and is recorded as a want

level_m.description: finished elevation of the paved/decked surface. A usable area on a slope is almost always cut or built to a level, so set this; omit only for a surface that genuinely follows the ground.

purpose.description: free text; sitting, dining, fire_pit, lawn, kitchen_garden, play, utility, landing are modelled and render as themselves, anything else draws as the nearest surface and is recorded as a want

size_override.description: True when the designer deliberately chose this plant's planning height and spread. Catalogue resync preserves these dimensions. Reset to catalogue size removes this flag; dimensions still undergo normal validation.

asset.description: A library MODEL NAME — a key of assets/plants/manifest.json, e.g. stone_pine — overriding the species regexes in viewer/src/assets.js. Not a filename: a bare name is what the preloaded, height-corrected path in assets.js looks up, and it is the only path that measures the model and puts its base on the ground.

form.description: Growth habit, for a species the regex tables in viewer/src/assets.js and viewer/src/plants.js do not name: rosette, grass, column, tree, palm, mat, mound, cane, vine, rush, strap, perennial, meadow. The last four exist because a Juncus, a Phormium, a yarrow and a poppy drift are four different silhouettes, and drawing them all as `mound` makes massed planting read as wallpaper. Free text is normalised ('spreading groundcover' -> mat, 'multi-trunk shrub' -> mound), and a species the tables DO name wins over it. Without it an unrecognised species falls to a size heuristic and renders as a generic blob, which is what would stop the plant library following a design to another climate.

foliage.description: Foliage COLOUR, when the plant is not simply green: silver, grey_green, blue_green, dark_green, bright_green, chartreuse, purple, bronze, variegated. Free text is normalised the same way form is ('silver-grey', 'blue-grey glaucous', 'dark glossy green'), and an explicit #rrggbb wins outright. Omit it and the plant takes the green ramp of its growth FORM, which every species of that form shares — half the plants in a garden can be `mound`, and that one ramp is 25 RGB units wide, 5.7% of the cube, so a silver lavender and a glossy dark toyon come out the same colour. A bare 'green' is deliberately ignored: it says no more than the form already does. Only the procedural path reads this; a plant big enough for a library model keeps that model's own leaf colour.

flower.description: Flower colour as #rrggbb. Optional; the viewer supplies the catalog default when absent. Use the named species or cultivar colour; foliage and flower colours are independent.

edges.description: retaining / border edging: a vertical strip standing along a line, used to hold a grade change or contain a bed

height_m.description: exposed height. The bounds here are the SHIPPED DEFAULTS so this file still validates on its own; agent.validate() overwrites them with site.constraints.edge_min_height_m and site.constraints.retain_limit_m before validating, because how tall a wall may stand is a rule about the address, not about the format. Above site.constraints.footing_threshold_m a face needs an engineered footing.

material.description: free text; corten_steel, aluminium, concrete, timber, stone, brick, dry_stone, boulder are modelled and render as themselves, anything else draws as the nearest surface and is recorded as a want

retains.description: which side the edge holds back

thickness_m.description: how thick the wall is built. Omit and it is agent.EDGE_SECTION[material].thickness_m, the same number viewer/src/design.js builds the solid from. It is not decoration: the setback between two stacked walls is measured face to face, so thickness spends it.

batter_deg.description: how far the face leans back into what it retains. Omit for the material default. A battered wall's top moves toward the terrace above it, so this spends setback too.

footing_depth_m.description: depth of footing below finished grade. Omit for the material default. A wall standing over site.constraints.footing_threshold_m with a stated footing shallower than its material needs is REJECTED — that is the one thing about a footing a drawing can check.

level_m.description: elevation the edge retains TO (top of wall). When set, exposed height varies with the ground along its run and height_m is the nominal figure.

steps.description: a flight of steps: the vocabulary for a route too steep to walk as a ramp. Put one across the stretch where a path runs over site.constraints.max_grade — the path is not graded as a ramp where a flight covers it.

spline.description: the line the flight runs down, top to bottom. Its ends give the fall the risers must absorb and its length gives the run they have to do it in.

riser_m.description: height of one step. The bounds here are the SHIPPED DEFAULTS so this file still validates on its own; agent.validate() overwrites the maximum with site.constraints.step_riser_max_m, because how tall a step may rise is a rule about the address, not about the format.

going_m.description: tread depth of one step. The minimum is overwritten by validate() with site.constraints.step_going_min_m. risers x going is the run the flight eats; a flight whose spline is shorter than that is rejected.

material.description: free text; corten_steel, aluminium, concrete, timber, stone, brick, dry_stone, boulder are modelled and render as themselves, anything else draws as the nearest surface and is recorded as a want

groups.description: Owner-authored groupings of design objects — 'the fire pit and its two retaining walls' as one thing that hides, locks and moves together. The key is `members`, which is what viewer saveGroups actually writes; this schema follows the code that writes a group, never an assumption about it, or every real group fails validation while a test built on the same assumption passes.

members.description: ids of the design objects in this group

alt_of.description: This group is one PROPOSAL in the named set; the others in that set are alternatives to it and are never built together. Measuring and judging resolve to the chosen one; the document keeps them all.

objects.description: Things a garden is made of that are not ground: a bench, a boulder, a stone lantern, a water basin, a pot, a fire pit, a screen, a pergola. `kind` is FREE TEXT on purpose — ask for what the design needs. A kind the library can build gets real geometry; one it cannot gets an honest placeholder at the size you asked for AND is recorded as a want, so a missing model is a work item rather than a silent downgrade. Never trim a design to what happens to be modelled.

kind.description: what it is, in your own words: 'stone lantern', 'tsukubai', 'olive jar', 'moon gate'

level_m.description: absolute elevation of the object's BASE, in the same datum as the terrain. Omit and it stands on the measured ground, which is the normal case. Set it to stand a thing on a plinth, a wall top or a deck — float_check still measures where it really ends up, so a lantern hanging in the air is reported, not silently accepted.

tilt_deg.description: lean, in degrees, about the object's own horizontal axis. 0 stands it plumb, which is the normal case. A set boulder leans; a screen or a gate does not. Taste is reported, never enforced — but float_check measures the geometry a lean actually produces, so a tilt that buries or floats the thing is still caught.

model.description: A path under assets/objects/ to a .glb the OWNER scanned — their own stone, their own pot. It beats the builder for that kind, the way a plant's `asset` beats the species table, and it is what lets a scan be placed rather than a preset that resembles one. The pattern forbids `..` and anything outside that directory: this string arrives in a document a model writes and reaches a loader in the browser. execute() additionally refuses a path that is not on disk, because a design naming a file nobody has draws nothing.

from.description: The design this one was saved out of. Written by Save-as; never inferred from a name. A fact about THIS document's origin, so it is replaced rather than inherited when a whole document is written.

alternatives.description: Which proposal is live, per set of mutually exclusive groups: {set_id: group_id}. Groups declare their set with alt_of. Membership has one home (the groups) and the choice has one home (here). An undeclared choice falls back to the first group of the set, never to showing both.
